issue: The caption names the first column 'Intel CPU' while the figure's own column header reads 'Intel GPU' and that column's Hardware box reads 'Discrete GPU or integrated GPU'. Caption and drawing disagree on what the first path is.
evidence: Caption: 'Intel CPU (torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL), Gaudi (hpu and its own stack), and client NPU (the OpenVINO NPU plugin).' Figure column header: 'Intel GPU'; Hardware box: 'Discrete GPU or integrated GPU'; Backend entry box: 'torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL'. torch.xpu is an Intel GPU (Xe) path, not a CPU path, so the caption's 'CPU' is a mislabel, not a second device class.
acceptance_test: Built PDF caption reads 'Intel GPU (torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL)' (or the figure header is changed to 'Intel CPU' and the Hardware box re-specified); the caption's three device names match the three figure column headers verbatim, in order.

issue: The dashed-line convention is defined twice with different meanings: the figure's own legend says 'Dashed: qualify the complete path', while the caption glosses dashed as 'dashed column outlines group each column (dashed = complete path, not interchangeable APIs)'. The caption drops the 'qualification' semantics on which the red gate box depends, so a reader who takes the caption as the legend reads the dashed lines as mere grouping and misses that the dashed path is what the gate qualifies.
evidence: Figure subtitle: 'Solid: dependencies. Dashed: qualify the complete path.' Caption: 'Solid arrows denote dependencies; dashed column outlines group each column (dashed = complete path, not interchangeable APIs).' The gate box below the columns is the only place the qualification meaning is realized.
acceptance_test: Caption and figure legend use one consistent definition of dashed (e.g. 'dashed = the path that must be qualified; solid = dependencies within the path'), and the caption states that the dashed path terminates in the qualification gate.

issue: Caption-to-figure semantic mismatch on gate structure: caption states 'three conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate' but the figure groups candidates (a) and (b) into a single shared 'OUTCOME — THROUGHPUT GATE' box and gives only (c) a separate quality-gate box. No candidate has 'its own' gate in the drawn layout.
evidence: Caption: 'three conditional candidates, each with its own open validation gate (not a settled verdict)'. Figure outcome row: left box 'CAPACITY SCREEN: (a) · (b) pass … THROUGHPUT GATE', right box 'QUALITY GATE (c)'. Candidates (a) and (b) share one gate box; (c) has a distinct box. The word 'each' implies three separate gate boxes.
acceptance_test: Either revise caption to 'candidates (a) and (b) share a throughput gate; candidate (c) awaits a quality gate' or redraw the outcome row with three per-candidate gate boxes.

issue: Caption names three gates 'MEM/THR/QUAL (memory fit · throughput at the SLO · quality)' but the figure labels the memory gate as 'CAPACITY SCREEN' rather than any MEM/memory-fit label. A reader mapping caption acronyms to figure boxes cannot find a box labeled MEM or memory-fit; the mapping CAPACITY SCREEN → MEM is unstated.
evidence: Caption: 'all tested against the same MEM/THR/QUAL gates (memory fit · throughput at the SLO · quality)'. Figure: left outcome box header reads 'OUTCOME — THROUGHPUT GATE' with sub-line 'CAPACITY SCREEN: (a) · (b) pass'. No box or label contains 'MEM' or 'memory fit'.
acceptance_test: Either add 'MEM' or 'memory fit' as a visible sub-label inside the capacity-screen box, or change the caption acronym list to match the figure's own gate names (CAPACITY/THR/QUAL).

issue: Grayscale distinguishability: the four stacked boxes use blue (requirements), orange (constraints), green (candidates), green (outcome), orange (quality gate). In grayscale the blue and green fills render as similar mid-tones and the two orange fills are identical. Structural labels (①②③④?) and distinct text provide redundancy, so the figure remains interpretable, but the color coding carries no independent grayscale signal.
evidence: Rendered page at 150 dpi: box fills are light blue, light orange, light green, light green, light orange. Converting to grayscale yields closely spaced mid-tones for blue vs green and identical tones for the two orange boxes.
acceptance_test: Convert figure to grayscale; verify that box roles remain distinguishable from fill tone alone or that a non-color cue (border style, icon, or explicit role tag) compensates. Current text labels partially compensate — confirm sufficiency at print size.

issue: The outcome area shows a throughput gate containing only (a) and (b), and a quality gate containing only (c). The caption says all three candidates are tested against the same MEM/THR/QUAL gates. The visual therefore implies that (c) is exempt from the throughput gate and that (a)/(b) are exempt from the quality gate.
evidence: Caption: three conditional candidates ... all tested against the same MEM/THR/QUAL gates (memory fit, throughput at the SLO, quality). Figure: OUTCOME - THROUGHPUT GATE box says CAPACITY SCREEN: (a) . (b) pass; QUALITY GATE (c) box says pending quality validation.
acceptance_test: Either show all three gates for each candidate, or relabel the two outcome boxes as the currently open gate per candidate and add an explicit note that every candidate must still pass MEM, THR, and QUAL; verify that (c) throughput status and (a)/(b) quality status are not visually omitted.

issue: The bottom line in the green OUTCOME - THROUGHPUT GATE box (~5 avg / ~19 peak hosts, headroom not demonstrated) is flush against the left border and may be clipped or visually cramped at print size.
evidence: Rendered page shows the tilde of ~5 starting at the left edge of the green box, with no visible internal padding.
acceptance_test: Add internal padding to the green box and re-render at print size; verify that no glyph touches or crosses the border and that the line remains fully legible in grayscale.

issue: The level-4 marker is placed outside (to the left of) the green OUTCOME box, whereas the level-1/2/3 markers are placed inside their boxes' title lines; the marker placement rule is inconsistent.
evidence: The circled 1 appears inside the blue box before 'REQUIREMENTS', 2 inside the orange box before 'CONSTRAINTS', 3 inside the green box before 'CANDIDATES'; the circled 4 appears in the left margin beside the green 'OUTCOME — THROUGHPUT GATE' box, not inside it.
acceptance_test: The circled 4 is rendered inside the level-4 box(es) (or a single consistent rule is applied to all four markers) so marker position is uniform across levels.

issue: Box colors carry no legend and are reused across levels with different roles (orange = CONSTRAINTS at level 2 and = QUALITY GATE (c) at level 4; green = CANDIDATES at level 3 and = OUTCOME—THROUGHPUT GATE at level 4), so color does not encode a consistent meaning.
evidence: The five boxes are colored blue / orange / green / green / orange; neither the figure nor the caption provides a color key, and the same hue denotes two different box types at different levels. (Grayscale is not the failure: the two level-4 boxes remain distinguishable by border and text.)
acceptance_test: Either a color key is added or the palette is made one-hue-per-role, so a reader can decode color without the caption; the two level-4 boxes stay distinguishable in grayscale.

issue: Three cells print a false arithmetic equation: the operator between the requirement and the per-unit rate is '+' where the derivation requires division. As printed, '368K + 19.8K = 18.6', '92,000 + 24,725 = 3.72', and '368,000 + 24,725 = 14.88' are all numerically false. The derived conclusions (19 hosts, 4 cards, 15 cards) are correct under division, so the defect is the operator, not the result.
evidence: Cell (a) peak: '~19 hosts (368K + 19.8K = 18.6, cell 19 before headroom)' — 368,000/19,800 = 18.59 -> 19. Cell (c) avg: '~4 H100 cards (92,000 + 24,725 = 3.72)' — 92,000/24,725 = 3.72. Cell (c) peak: '~15 H100 cards (368,000 + 24,725 = 14.88), before headroom' — 368,000/24,725 = 14.88. The requirement values 92,000 and 368,000 tok/s are independently confirmed by Fig 12.1 (10 avg / 40 peak rps x 9,200 in-tokens).
acceptance_test: All three parentheticals print a true equation using a division operator ('368K / 19.8K = 18.6', '92,000 / 24,725 = 3.72', '368,000 / 24,725 = 14.88'), and a re-derivation of each cell from the stated requirement and rate reproduces the printed host/card count.

issue: The lead-in paragraph labels the rates as 'per-host' and then states '~24,700 tok/s for the 8-GPU node', but column (c) consumes 24,725 tok/s per H100 card, and the same parenthetical computes the node aggregate as 8 x 24,725 = 197,800. The unit of the rate is therefore stated inconsistently (per-host vs per-card) and the node figure is given two different values (24,700 vs 197,800). A reader who takes 'per-host' literally computes 92,000/197,800 = 0.47 hosts for (a) and 92,000/24,725 = 3.72 cards for (c) — i.e. a fleet count off by roughly an order of magnitude in column (a).
evidence: Lead-in: 'Host counts are an illustrative capacity screen from the fixed per-host prefill rates (~19,800 tok/s for the 70B candidates; ~24,700 tok/s for the 8-GPU node; the 8-GPU node, 8 x 24,725 = 197,800, not this layout)'. Column (c) cells divide the requirement by 24,725 and report 'cards', not hosts; column (a) divides by 19,800 and reports 'hosts'.
acceptance_test: The lead-in states the unit of each rate unambiguously (e.g. '~19,800 tok/s per 70B host; ~24,725 tok/s per H100 card, so an 8-GPU node offers ~197,800 tok/s aggregate — not the layout used here'), and every table cell's divisor is labelled with the same unit as the cell's output (hosts vs cards).

issue: The two prefill-capacity row labels contain an undefined token: 'avg r2K tok/s' and 'peak r2K tok/s'. 'r2K' is not defined anywhere on the page and cannot denote a value, since the two rows carry different requirements (92,000 and 368,000 tok/s). If the source string is 'req', the built PDF has a rendering/encoding artifact; if the source literally reads 'r2K', it is an unexplained abbreviation in a row header.
evidence: Row labels as rendered: 'Prefill capacity (hosts or cards), avg r2K tok/s' and 'Prefill capacity (hosts or cards), peak r2K tok/s'. Cell derivations use 92,000 tok/s (avg) and 368,000 tok/s (peak), consistent with Fig 12.1's '10 avg / 40 peak rps' and '9.2K-in'.
acceptance_test: Row labels read 'required tok/s' (or state the requirement explicitly, e.g. 'avg req 92K tok/s' / 'peak req 368K tok/s'); the string 'r2K' does not appear in the built PDF; the label is unambiguous without reference to the cell contents.

issue: The figure uses 'SLO' for two different things in adjacent boxes: the REQUIREMENTS box ends 'SLO = quality', while the CONSTRAINTS box begins 'SLO: throughput at target load'. The caption resolves the intent (throughput gate for a and b, quality gate for c), so the figure's own box 1 contradicts both box 2 and the caption. A reader who takes 'SLO = quality' as the canonical workload's SLO will misread the whole gate structure.
evidence: Box 1: 'canonical workload ~2,000 users, 10 avg / 40 peak rps, 9.2K-in/300-out, SLO = quality'. Box 2: 'SLO: throughput at target load (10 avg / 40 peak rps, 9.2K-in/300-out)'. Caption: 'each must measure its gate (throughput for a,b; quality for c) at the target load (Chs. 14-17)'.
acceptance_test: Box 1 states the workload's SLO in the same terms as box 2 (e.g. 'SLO: TTFT/TPOT at target load'), and the word 'quality' appears in the figure only where the quality gate (candidate c) is introduced; caption and boxes agree on which gate applies to which candidate.

issue: The OUTCOME box reports a single host count for both throughput-gate candidates: '~5 avg / ~19 peak hosts'. Table 12-3 shows those numbers are the prefill pool only for candidate (b), which additionally requires a separate decode pool ('decode pool sized to 3K tok/s agg / 12K tok/s peak'). Read as applying to (a) and (b) alike, the figure understates (b)'s host requirement by the entire decode pool.
evidence: Fig 12.1 outcome box: 'CAPACITY SCREEN: (a) - (b) pass / validation open until Chs. 14-17 / ~5 avg / ~19 peak hosts, headroom not demonstrated'. Table 12-3 (PDF 237 / printed 217): (a) '~5 hosts' avg, '~19 hosts' peak, 'Decode pool sizing: none - decode shares the host'; (b) 'prefill pool ~5 hosts' avg, 'prefill pool ~19 hosts, before headroom', 'decode pool sized to 3K tok/s agg / 12K tok/s peak'.
acceptance_test: The outcome box either reports per-candidate host counts ('(a) ~5 avg / ~19 peak hosts; (b) ~5 prefill hosts avg / ~19 peak + decode pool') or explicitly labels the single number as the prefill-pool screen only, with a pointer to Table 12-3 for the decode pool.

issue: The CONSTRAINTS box's second line, 'memory fit per host - quality gate', conflates a capacity constraint with a gate type. Memory fit is a capacity constraint (it is what the throughput/capacity screen checks), while the quality gate applies only to candidate (c) per the caption and the figure's own '? QUALITY GATE (c)' box. As written, the constraint list implies that memory fit is validated by a quality gate.
evidence: Box 2: 'SLO: throughput at target load (10 avg / 40 peak rps, 9.2K-in/300-out) / memory fit per host - quality gate'. Box 4: 'OUTCOME - THROUGHPUT GATE ... ? QUALITY GATE (c): pending quality validation'.
acceptance_test: Box 2 lists 'memory fit per host' as a capacity constraint without attaching 'quality gate' to it, and the quality gate appears in the figure only in the candidate-(c) outcome box; a reader can state which constraint each gate tests.

issue: The 'DE-ESCALATE: privacy - sovereignty - cost' label is placed at the top of the figure, immediately to the right of the upward red escalation arrowhead, while de-escalation is represented by the separate downward blue dashed arrow on the far right. The label is therefore visually attached to the escalation arrow it does not describe, and a reader scanning the top of the figure can plausibly conclude that the top of the ladder is 'de-escalate' or that the red arrow is the de-escalation path.
evidence: Figure: large red arrow pointing up (escalation) with 'DE-ESCALATE: privacy - sovereignty - cost' printed to the right of its head; a thin blue dashed arrow pointing down at the far right, unlabeled in place. Caption: 'Escalation (red) fires when demand, KV residency, or goodput outgrows a tier; de-escalation (blue) fires on privacy, sovereignty, and cost'.
acceptance_test: The de-escalation label sits within the vertical span of the blue dashed arrow (e.g. beside its midpoint or its lower end) and is visually separated from the red arrowhead; no label text for one direction is adjacent to the arrowhead of the other direction.

issue: The caption contains a broken escape artifact: 'Rungs refine the $13 tiers' where a section reference is intended. The literal '$13' is visible in the built PDF and reads as a stray dollar sign rather than a section pointer.
evidence: Caption: 'Rungs refine the $13 tiers: Single GPU -> Local edge, Single host -> Server, Multi-host -> Cluster, Cluster/fleet -> Hyperscale fleet. [ILLUSTRATIVE conceptual]'.
acceptance_test: The built PDF caption renders 'Rungs refine the Sec. 13 tiers' (or the book's chosen section-reference style); the source contains no unescaped '$' in this sentence, and the rendered glyph is a section mark, not a currency symbol.

issue: Caption wording error: 'scale-down decisions should also reference utilizations (sustained low load on a tier)'. 'utilizations' is a plural noun where the singular 'utilization' is meant, and the parenthetical then defines it as a single quantity.
evidence: Caption: '...but scale-down decisions should also reference utilizations (sustained low load on a tier), failure domain (a smaller tier has a smaller blast radius), operations burden (fewer hosts to run), and SLO margin (headroom to absorb a burst without breaching the SLO).'
acceptance_test: Caption reads 'utilization (sustained low load on a tier)'; the list items are all singular quantities.

issue: The caption's causal order for the final stage contradicts the figure's arrows: the figure draws Selection -> TCO+SLO gate -> deployed (the gate is applied to the selection), but the caption says the benchmark results 'pass the TCO + SLO gate to the deployed system, feeding selection and TCO' (the gate feeds selection).
evidence: Figure arrows: gray Survivors->Selection, green Selection->'TCO + SLO gate', green 'TCO + SLO gate'->'deployed'. Caption clause: 'whose results pass the TCO + SLO gate to the deployed system, feeding selection and TCO.' The same-page prose (14.6) also orders it as bench drives the choice, then TCO downstream, matching the figure, not the caption.
acceptance_test: The caption's final-stage wording matches the figure's arrow direction (selection is the input to the TCO+SLO gate, whose output is the deployed system), or the figure's arrows are changed to match the caption.
